Net effect: a tower covering the spawn spends about a second of fire per monster into a life reset, and because the emerging monster is the NEAREST instance it is that tower's PREFERRED target. Two things to settle: was the reset meant to make the emerge untargetable (then the monster should not be findable - find_all_range should skip it), or should the damage persist (then drop the reset)? Either way it makes tower placement a real decision, so the sim has to model it rather than assume it away.  DECIDED 2026-10-18: DAMAGE PERSISTS. The reset is deleted (scr_zombie_emerge now only calls scr_changeState at step 60), so the card's two options resolved to the second one. Why not "make the emerge untargetable" instead: a monster that is not shootable is a monster the player cannot learn to pre-fire, and hiding it from find_all_range would have made tower placement LESS decisive, not more. A monster killed during the emerge now walks for one frame and dies on the first path frame, because scr_zomb_death still runs from scr_zombie_path - that one-frame delay is the only visible trace, and it is why the HP bar can show 0 through the last emerge frame. |

The cycle a tower waits out is now attack_cycle = tower_cycle_frames(rate, return) + time_offset = fire period + return animation + stagger, and it is DELIBERATE: the swing is capped at tower_swing_seconds() (0.35s) instead of being as long as the period, so a fast tower fires the moment it finishes returning - its delivered rate is exactly what the closed form and the sim assume - while a slow one strikes in a third of a second and spends the rest of its period idle. The 0.25s return is inside the cycle on purpose: charging it is what keeps the shop card comparable with the sim. What is left is a DOC sentence, not a code question - economy.md 4.2 still describes the old cycle, and that is tracked by docs-status-quo-decisions. |

Options: a per-wave clear bonus that does not depend on kills, partial pay for a leak, or leaving it as the intended punishment. Measure it with the CURVE panel after the ceiling change: note the money and the bite on the wave after the first leak.  DECIDED 2026-10-18: PARTIAL PAY, HALF A KILL, applied by scr_kill_money(base, wave, ramp, 0.5) in lose_life. Not a per-wave clear bonus: that would have paid a player for losing, in every wave, including the ones they cleared - a leak is still the only thing that pays it. Not "leave it as punishment" either: the first leak then removed the income needed to answer the next wave, which is the starvation the card was filed for. THE TRAP (LL-061): halving the ROUNDED payout pays 0 for a 1-money creature - floor(1 x 0.5) = 0 - so the scale goes into the rule before its floor and rides money_carry. |
